limitations_and_boundaries: The study primarily uses HeLa-Kyoto cells; generalizability to other cell types is partially addressed but not exhaustive.
The AFM-based confinement assay uses a flat cantilever, which may not fully replicate the complex 3D geometries in vivo.
The nuclear ruler model is based on a specific threshold height (~5 µm) and may vary with cell type and nuclear size.
The role of other endomembranes (e.g., ER) in cytoplasts at extreme confinement is not fully characterized.
Long-term effects of nuclear deformation on gene expression and cell fate are not explored.

To test whether cells would also adapt their cortical actomyosin contractility to the degree of environmental confinement in a context that more closely recapitulates in vivo settings, we examined human fibrosarcoma cells HT1080 infiltrating three-dimensional (3D) cell-derived matrices (CDMs) (Fig. 1F). Cortical recruitment of myosin in these cells linearly scaled with the self-imposed smallest dimension of the cell (Fig. 1F), thus validating our AFM-based observations.
